name: Linear Algebra
description: Matrices, determinants, linear systems, vector spaces, eigenvalues and decompositions for GATE.

nodes.name: Vectors
nodes.desc: Vectors, dot product, length and angle, and the geometry of linear combinations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute with vectors, using dot products for length and angle, and interpret linear combinations geometrically.

nodes.name: Matrices
nodes.desc: Matrix algebra: addition, multiplication, transpose, trace, powers and commuting matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to carry out matrix algebra confidently, including products, transposes, traces and powers, and recognise when matrices commute.

nodes.name: Special matrices
nodes.desc: Symmetric, skew-symmetric, triangular, idempotent, nilpotent, orthogonal, projection and rotation matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise special classes of matrices and use their defining properties to simplify computations.

nodes.name: Determinants
nodes.desc: Cofactor expansion, properties under row operations, and determinants of structured matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to evaluate determinants by cofactor expansion and row operations and exploit structure in special matrices.

nodes.name: Inverse & adjoint
nodes.desc: Invertibility, the adjoint formula, singular matrices and inverse identities.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide when a matrix is invertible and compute inverses using the adjoint formula and standard identities.

nodes.name: Rank
nodes.desc: Row echelon form, rank, and how rank behaves under products and sums.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute the rank of a matrix from its echelon form and bound the rank of products and sums.
topics: Row echelon and reduced row echelon form

nodes.name: Linear systems
nodes.desc: Ax = b: consistency, unique versus infinitely many solutions, and the rank test.
nodes.summary: You will be able to determine whether Ax = b has no solution, a unique solution or infinitely many using the rank test.

nodes.name: Gaussian elimination
nodes.desc: Row reduction, back substitution and solving systems by hand.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve linear systems by hand using row reduction to echelon form followed by back substitution.

nodes.name: LU decomposition
nodes.desc: Factorising A = LU and using it to solve systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to factor a matrix as A = LU and solve systems efficiently with forward and back substitution.

nodes.name: Homogeneous systems
nodes.desc: Ax = 0, trivial versus non-trivial solutions, and null spaces.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide when Ax = 0 has non-trivial solutions and describe the null space with a basis.

nodes.name: Vector spaces
nodes.desc: Vector spaces and subspaces over a field, span and linear independence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to verify the vector space axioms, identify subspaces and test sets of vectors for span and linear independence.
topics: Vector space axioms over a field
Span of a set of vectors

nodes.name: Basis & dimension
nodes.desc: Bases, dimension, the four fundamental subspaces and the rank–nullity theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find bases and dimensions of the four fundamental subspaces and apply the rank-nullity theorem.
topics: Null space and left null space

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.desc: Orthogonal and orthonormal bases, projections and Gram–Schmidt.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build orthonormal bases with Gram-Schmidt and compute orthogonal projections onto subspaces.
topics: Projection onto a vector and a subspace

nodes.name: Eigenvalues
nodes.desc: The characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues, and their links to trace and determinant.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find eigenvalues from the characteristic polynomial and relate their sum and product to trace and determinant.
topics: Eigenvalues of A inverse and A^k

nodes.name: Eigenvectors
nodes.desc: Eigenvectors and eigenspaces, algebraic and geometric multiplicity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute eigenvectors and eigenspaces and compare algebraic and geometric multiplicities of eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Cayley–Hamilton
nodes.desc: Every matrix satisfies its characteristic equation; computing powers and inverses with it.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the Cayley-Hamilton theorem to compute matrix powers, inverses and polynomials in a matrix.
topics: Computing the inverse from the characteristic equation

nodes.name: Eigen of special forms
nodes.desc: Eigenvalues of symmetric, triangular, rank-one, block and projection matrices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read off or quickly derive eigenvalues of symmetric, triangular, rank-one, block and projection matrices.
topics: Block diagonal and block triangular matrices

nodes.name: Diagonalisation
nodes.desc: When A = PDP⁻¹ exists, orthogonal diagonalisation of symmetric matrices, and matrix powers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test whether a matrix is diagonalisable, orthogonally diagonalise symmetric matrices and compute matrix powers.

nodes.name: Quadratic forms
nodes.desc: Quadratic forms, definiteness and the Rayleigh quotient.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write quadratic forms as symmetric matrices, classify their definiteness and bound them with the Rayleigh quotient.

nodes.name: SVD
nodes.desc: Singular values, the singular value decomposition, and low-rank approximation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute and interpret the singular value decomposition and use it for low-rank approximation.
topics: Singular values from A transpose A
